steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: An income statement (profit and loss account) shows revenue, costs, and profit over a period: revenue - cost of sales = gross profit; gross profit - expenses = net profit. | Key Fact: A balance sheet shows what a business OWNS (assets) and OWES (liabilities) at a specific date: assets = liabilities + capital. It's a snapshot of financial position. | Key Fact: Gross profit margin = (gross profit / revenue) x 100. It shows how efficiently the business produces its goods - a higher margin means lower production costs relative to selling price. | Key Fact: Net profit margin = (net profit / revenue) x 100. It shows overall profitability after ALL costs - a higher margin means better overall cost control.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Calculate the gross profit margin and net profit margin for a business with revenue £200,000, cost of sales £120,000, and expenses £50,000. | Explain what a current ratio of 0.8 means for a business and suggest what it should do. | Evaluate why financial ratios are useful but also have limitations when comparing business performance.
